title: Ordinary Finite Twist Composition
statement:
Canonical section variables and instances are those of the attached Lean module.

theorem ordinaryFiniteLinePullback_comp
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZ : IsUnit (N : Γ(Z, ⊤))) (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) :
    (t.line (f ≫ g) hZ).hom =
      (upperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g).hom.app
        (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine Z N A hA) ≫
      (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).map (t.line g hZ).hom ≫ (t.line f hY).hom

theorem ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback_comp
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZ : IsUnit (N : Γ(Z, ⊤))) (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) :
    (leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g).hom.app
        ((ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA Z)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
      (ordinaryFinitePullback A f).map
        (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t g hZ).hom ≫
      (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t f hY).hom =
        (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t (f ≫ g) hZ).hom

theorem ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback_comp_of_eq
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (fg : X ⟶ Z)
    (hfg : fg = f ≫ g) (hZ : IsUnit (N : Γ(Z, ⊤))) (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) :
    (leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f g fg hfg).hom.app
        ((ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA Z)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
      (ordinaryFinitePullback A f).map
        (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t g hZ).hom ≫
      (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t f hY).hom =
        (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t fg hZ).hom

proof.text: Normalization on roots and pure tensors identifies the specified twist transport with the canonical normalized transport, giving its sheaf-line composition law. Reuse the exact degree-zero composition and exact-to-derived comparison calculations of FiniteP1TwistedUnitBaseChange. Shift the exact composition equation by shifted_composite_comparison. Naturality and inverse-isomorphism cancellation transport this equation along the canonical total-derived-to-exact comparisons. The retained shiftedLine_eq identifies the specified maps with these composites.
